result:
Only this one `AgentTest` file exists, and the full suite via `./_tools/test.sh` passes (56/56).

Summary: I wrote `WordUtilsAgentTest` (56 tests) covering `capitalize`, `capitalizeFully`, `containsAllWords`, `initials`, `swapCase`, `uncapitalize`, `wrap`, and the public constructor, including null/empty/boundary cases, custom delimiters, and the custom `wrapOn` pattern.

During development, 4 tests initially failed, but in every case the test itself was wrong, not the code:
- The `wrap` javadoc's worked example for `wrapLongWords=true` ("https://commons.apach\ne.org") doesn't match the stated contract that `wrapLength` is "the column to wrap the words at" — hand-tracing shows the code correctly cuts at exactly 20 columns ("https://commons.apac\nhe.org"); the table entry is stale documentation, not a code bug.
- `capitalizeFully(*, null)` / `uncapitalize(*, null)` javadoc tables claim `= *` (unchanged), but this contradicts the single-arg overloads, which delegate to the exact same call and are documented to capitalize/uncapitalize using whitespace — another stale doc line, not matching actual (and self-consistent) behavior.
- `swapCase("hello world")` produces `"HELLO WORLD"`, not `"Hello World"` — this follows directly from the documented algorithm (only the first letter of each word becomes title case; other lowercase letters become uppercase), so my original expectation was simply incorrect.

No tests remain failing — I found no genuine bugs in `WordUtils` itself, only documentation/table inconsistencies in the javadoc that don't match the class's own self-consistent, documented rules.
